C0.quote: Ranking the participants of a tournament has applications in voting
C0.note: Eligible: tournament ranking is studied as a social choice procedure; the input tournament can arise from majority voting.

C1.loc: Abstract, p. 1236; Section 3, p. 1238; Section 6, p. 1241
C1.quote: through the axiomatic method of social choice theory
C1.note: AX is the largest share of main results. AL applies to NP-hardness/tractability and the interleaving algorithm; OT applies to the probabilistic MLE model.

C2.1.quote: An operator φ assigns each tournament K a pair

C2.2.quote: K is an m × n matrix with Kab ∈ {0, 1}
C2.2.note: The input is a matrix of pairwise match results between the two sides.

C2.3.quote: x beats y if a majority of voters prefer x over y
C2.3.note: The paper refers to voters' preferences when explaining the voting interpretation of tournaments, though these preferences are not modelled individually.

C2.4.quote: x beats y if a majority of voters prefer x over y
C2.4.note: The input tournament K is distinct from the voters' preferences that may generate it.

C3.1.note: No analysis models voters submitting inputs that differ from their held attitudes.

C3.2.note: No statement found that voters submit their held preferences.

C3.3.note: C3.2 is NOT-STATED, so C3.3 does not apply.

C4.1.note: Although C2.2 includes PAIR, the paper does not use utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost, distortion, or intensity of preference for voters.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.note: No result evaluates outcomes by welfare, efficiency, voter satisfaction, representation, proportionality, or distortion.

VOT.note: No voters modelled as agents taking actions; voters' preferences are mentioned only in the introductory interpretation.

CAN.note: Players A and B are ranked alternatives/participants but take no actions in the formal model.

ORG.note: No organiser, chair, or election authority acts in the model.

DES.note: No rule/mechanism designer whose choice or objective is modelled explicitly.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two stakeholder types are present by the C6 definition.

C8.1.note: No present type is STRAT or MIXED, so no solution concept applies.
